# FDG3018

> DO use a common name, such as *value* or *item*, rather than repeating the type name, in the rare cases when an identifier has no semantic meaning and the type of the parameter is not important.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.2.3 Avoiding Language-Specific Names.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1720
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test none
- Status: verified

CA1720 reports parameter names that are built-in or CLR type names, such as 'double' or 'int32'; it does not see names of other types, such as 'stream'.

## From the book

The following is a good example of methods of a class that support writing a variety of data types into a stream:

```csharp
void Write(double value);
void Write(float value);
void Write(short value);
```
